messages:
Maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing 'skyline' dependency refactor for console query layer. Goal: decouple dashboard render graph from authz/ingest hot paths so we can reduce p95 latency under fanout. Sketch below, looking for concerns on RBAC implications and rollout plan. :wave:

Jon: high-level ok. Can you paste the proposed interface? main concern is RBAC causing N extra calls per tile and amplification under large dashboards. p95 already spikes with /dash/render when we hit 20 widgets. :grimacing:

Maya: sure, rough API prototype:```ts
// new facade that returns prepped tile payloads and a per-tile auth token
interface QuerySkyline {
  prepareDashboard(dashboardId: string, ctx: RequestCtx): Promise<SkylineHandle>;
  fetchTiles(handle: SkylineHandle, tileIds: string[]): Promise<TilePayload[]>;
}

// SkylineHandle contains a short-lived auth blob to avoid repeated RBAC calls
```

Lena: interesting. So idea is move RBAC to prepareDashboard and issue per-handle short-lived proofs instead of per-tile checks? That would cut per-tile auth from ~8ms to 0 if cached, but we need threat model review. How do we revoke if permission changes mid-request? :thinking:

Maya: correct — handle TTL is small (configurable, default 2s). We still validate user->dashboard access at prepare time and embed allowed columns/filters into the handle. For mid-request changes, worst-case we allow the current in-flight render to finish; subsequent requests re-evaluate. Thoughts on compliance?

Priya: product question — any UI changes? This should be invisible, but we need to ensure canary doesn't change ordering/timestamps for widgets (some customers depend on stable render order). Also perf wins should be measurable in the UX telemetry.

Jon: two technical concerns: 1) complexity of handle lifecycle — we must avoid memory leaks if handles are stored; prefer stateless handles (signed JWT-style blob). 2) caching semantics: if handle embeds allowed columns, it's basically a capability token. Need HMAC + short TTL.

Maya: agreed — plan is stateless signed handle (no server-side storage). Signing key rotated with KID and validators do signature + revocation-list consult (revocation expected rare).

Lena: revocation-list hits could add latency. Suggest we make revocation-list a Bloom filter in memory and update via streaming config to all nodes. If revocation notification midday, we can invalidate new handles. That avoids synchronous DB checks.

Jon: another perf worry — how does this interact with batching at the query-executor? If each tile has its own per-tile path, we must ensure fetchTiles can request multiple tiles in one exec call so backend can batch. Example shape:```json
{ "handle": "<signed>", "tiles": ["t1","t2","t3"], "opts": {"maxBatchMs": 8} }
```

Maya: yes fetchTiles supports multi-tile fetch to keep executor-level batching intact. We'll add a route that accepts up to N tile ids and returns ordered payloads. MaxBatchMs allows controlled microbatching.

Priya: rollout plan? We should do staged migration: new facade in shadow mode -> canary render for low-volume customers -> opt-in beta -> full rollout. Add telemetry flags to compare old vs new p95/p99 and correctness diffs on a per-dashboard basis.

Maya: proposed checklist: 1) implement QuerySkyline facade + handle signing 2) add shadow mode in staging + compare outputs 3) run synthetic fanout tests (20/100 widgets) 4) canary 1% of traffic with fallback to old path 5) increase canary and monitor SLOs: target p95 < 250ms, p99 < 800ms for render route 6) enable full rollout.

Lena: +1, but add safety circuit: if canary sees >5% error delta or p95 regression >20% in 5m window, auto rollback. Also ensure logs include handle KID so we can trace auth decisions.

Jon: implementation note: add feature flag to gate signed-handle enforcement. During rollout, tokens accepted from both old and new path. And make sure executor validates tile-level permission subset derived from handle — avoid full re-eval.

Maya: will draft an RFC with diagrams and perf numbers. Quick ask: anyone opposed to the capability-token approach for RBAC? Call out other attack vectors now.

Priya: no strong objections, but loop in security for threat modeling before canary. I'll file a follow-up with PM/PD.

Lena: also add audit events when handles are created and when tiles are fetched (include hashed dashboard id). Compliance needs that for customer audits.

Jon: code-level nit: keep signature algorithm as ed25519 for speed. Avoid RSA.

Maya: noted. I'll update the draft and assign owners. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging (skyline-v0.1) — watch staging-render-* metrics.
